title: Not east or west
hookLine: righteousness is not turning your face east or west, but belief, giving, keeping promises, patience (2:177)

cards: A few pages back, al-Baqarah told of the qiblah turning: the direction of prayer moved from Jerusalem to Mecca, and some people argued about it loudly. Which way is right? Which way is holy?

An argument about a direction can run a long time without anyone having to change how they live. Further on in the same surah, one verse steps over the whole argument with a single sentence. Today: birr.

teach.b: Verse one hundred seventy-seven, in Pickthall's words: “It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West.”
The word is birr: righteousness, goodness, devotion, the same word Muslims use for kindness to parents, birr al-walidayn. Then the verse says what birr is, in a long, concrete list.
Belief in God, the Last Day, the angels, the book, the prophets. Giving wealth, though you love it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and to free those in bondage.
Establishing the prayer and paying the zakat. Keeping your promises when you make them. And patience in poverty, in sickness, and in the moment of danger.
Commentators read one phrase two ways: giving wealth 'ala hubbihi can mean despite loving it, or out of love for God. Both readings have their teachers.
The verse doesn't say direction doesn't matter; Muslims still face the Kaaba when they pray. It says facing the right way isn't, by itself, goodness.
Goodness is belief that shows up as giving, praying, keeping your word, and holding steady when things go wrong.
Look back at the week: builders who prayed for people not yet born, a father asking what his sons would keep, a middle people, remembrance, loss, the clouds. Each day was a piece of this one list.

how: Muslims often cite 2:177 as a summary of faith in practice: belief together with charity, prayer, zakat, keeping promises and patience; the same word, birr, names kindness to parents.

o: facing the correct direction, toward Mecca, in prayer
righteousness, goodness: belief shown in what you do
a yearly charity given from savings, like zakat

after the turning of the qiblah

games.q: people are arguing loudly about which direction is holy. what does al-Baqarah 2:177 say?
o: righteousness isn't the direction; it's belief, giving, prayer, promises, patience.
games.why: it steps over the argument: it is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West. then it lists what is.

practice: Think back over the last week to what you said you'd do: call back, send the file, fix the shelf, visit, pay someone back.
Find one you haven't kept yet, and picture keeping it in the plainest way, holding the decision quietly, like something already done.

wordCard.voice: Birr. Righteousness, goodness, devotion. Al-Baqarah says it's not facing east or west, but belief, giving, prayer, keeping promises, and patience. Today's word.
